name: naive_vague_problem
description: NAIVE SUITE. A first-time caller who does not know how the phone system is organised and describes their problem the way real people do - vaguely, out of order, without volunteering tidy fields. Tests whether triage can classify natural speech instead of speech that has been shaped to fit it.
_how_to_read_a_failure: Read this before touching the persona. Every other scenario in testing/scenarios is scripted: the caller is told its goals in order and often the exact words to say ('always include the words a real person'). Those suites verify that a mechanism works. This suite verifies that a PERSON can get through, and it only does that as long as the persona stays unrehearsed. So: a HARD failure means the caller hit a dead end - that is a bug. A SOFT failure is a friction finding to triage, NOT a test to fix. Do not make the caller more cooperative to turn a soft failure green; that is exactly how the scripted suites drifted. Precedent, 2026-08-20: a caller was talked over mid-answer and misrouted to the AI specialist, and the persona was edited to stop being interruptible rather than the interruption being treated as the defect. naive_interrupts exists because of that.

setup._comment: An agent is available and will answer, so 'nobody was there' can never be mistaken for a friction signal. Whether the caller ends up with a human at all is left entirely to the caller and the product - no assertion here requires it.

missions.label: a first-time caller who does not know what to ask for
missions._persona_comment: Deliberately contains no required phrases, no ordered goals, and no instruction that would help the product's detectors fire. The only imperative rules are termination rules, which are harness hygiene (cost control) rather than character - they are marked as such so nobody mistakes them for licence to add more.
missions.persona: You are a person phoning a company because something you bought a few weeks ago has stopped working properly. You have never called them before and you have no idea how their phone system is set up - you do not know what departments they have, what an 'AI assistant' would be, or what information they are going to want from you. You are not a confident or well-organised phone caller. Behave like someone who has not rehearsed: explain your situation in your own words, a bit out of order, and mention things as they occur to you. Do not volunteer neat structured details like model numbers or account numbers unless you are actually asked for them, and if you are asked for something you do not have to hand, say so. If you do not understand a question, say you do not understand rather than guessing at an answer. If you are offered a choice between options you do not recognise, it is fine to ask what the difference is. You are perfectly willing to be helped by whoever can actually help you - you just do not know who that is. TERMINATION (harness hygiene, not part of the character): if you have heard four hold announcements, or roughly 14 exchanges have gone by, say goodbye and use end_call. Never mention that you are an AI or that this is a test.
missions.post_prompt: Report the call as ONLY a raw JSON object - no prose, no markdown fences. Answer as the CALLER, about your own experience, honestly - including when the experience was poor. Keys exactly: mission (string, 'naive_vague_problem'), got_helped (boolean - did you end up somewhere that could actually help you), reached (one of 'human','human_queue','ai_specialist','callback','still_with_receptionist','nowhere'), misrouted (boolean - true if you were sent somewhere you had not asked for), understood_what_was_asked (boolean - did you understand every question you were asked), knew_what_the_options_meant (boolean - when you were offered choices, did you understand what you were choosing between; false if you had to guess), had_to_repeat_yourself (boolean), times_you_repeated (integer), was_talked_over (boolean - did the agent start speaking while you were still answering), long_awkward_silence (boolean), would_a_real_person_have_hung_up (boolean - would an ordinary impatient human have given up on this call), most_confusing_moment (string - one short sentence, or empty if none), turns (integer), notes (short string).

assertions.label: the caller returned a structured verdict
the agent's side of the call was captured
HARD BAR: the caller did not hit a dead end
assertions._comment: The only substantive hard assertion in this suite, and the whole point of it. Any of these destinations is a pass - which path a naive caller takes is theirs and the product's business, not the test's. 'nowhere' and 'still_with_receptionist' are the failures: the caller went round in circles and never got anywhere.

assertions.label: OBSERVABILITY: the call had been classified by the time we looked
assertions._comment: SOFT, and only an observability signal. end_reason is written ASYNCHRONOUSLY and is frequently still None when the runner reads the report - the first live suite run had it None on three of four calls, and one of those was only resolved 26 minutes later by the call_watchdog reaping it ('status=assigned age=1556s exceeds cap 900s' -> end_reason='missed'). Asserting it HARD was simply wrong and manufactured three fake dead ends. There is no objective end-state signal available at poll time, so `reached` is deliberately left as the single hard bar rather than propping it up with a weaker companion.

assertions.label: FRICTION: the caller was not sent somewhere they had not asked for
assertions._comment: The interruption defect in one assertion. A fragmentary answer that names no option makes _human_request_evidence read ABSENT, and the caller is routed to the AI specialist by design - correct code, wrong outcome for the person, and invisible unless something asks them.

assertions.label: FRICTION: the caller understood every question they were asked
FRICTION: the caller knew what the offered options meant
assertions._comment: Watch this one. 'a human specialist, or our AI assistant' is offered to people who have never been told what either is, and a caller who picks by guessing is a misroute waiting to happen.

assertions.label: FRICTION: the caller did not have to repeat themselves
FRICTION: the caller was not talked over
FRICTION: an ordinary impatient human would not have given up
